newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht down, rumour of central bank action.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht down, rumour of central bank action.

text.p: The Thai baht slid on Monday amid end of year position squaring by some foreign investors as well as on selling to buy the strong dollar, foreign exchange dealers said.
They told Reuters the central bank was rumoured to have intervened twice on Monday in Singapore by increasing dollar supply in the market at lower than market offered rates to stem the baht decline.

"We heard the Bank of Thailand intervened twice in Singapore when the baht fell sharply," said a treasurer at a foreign bank. "Some investors are trying to test and see how far the central bank will go to defend the baht."
Thai central bank officials were unavailable for comment.

At 0858 GMT, the baht was traded at 25.610-25.615 to the dollar after briefly falling as low as 25.620 in early afternoon trade, dealers said. This was in sharp contrast to the early morning when it was quoted at around 25.586-25.590.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the dollar/baht mid-rate at 25.56 against 25.53 on Friday.
Dealers in Singapore said the central bank had intervened twice on Monday in that market.
"They (Bank of Thailand) came in once this morning at the 25.59 level and again this afternoon, probably around the 25.605 level," said a senior dealer with a Thai bank in Singapore.

He said it was difficult to estimate the amount of dollars sold, adding: "They called a number of banks but I believe each was a small amount only, maybe about $20 to $30 (million) through each bank."

He said the intervention was probably aimed at slowing down the baht's decline. "Being the year-end, there's a lot of outflow of funds. They cannot really stop it. But if it moves a little too fast, they would just come in to slow down the move."
The dollar was likely to face resistance at around 25.630 and 25.650 would provide a very strong barrier, he added.

Dealers said the recent strong demand for the U.S. unit in the market was because some market players, especially offshore banks in Singapore, tried to cover their dollar short positions ahead of the year-end.

"So far, I heard no rumour behind the heavy buying of the dollar against the baht today. But some major foreign banks were seen trying to buy the dollar to cover their short positions," said one senior dealer at a Thai bank.
